record.program_name: City of Madera Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA), 2019-2023 five-year plan
record.typical_award_size: 2022 PLHA award of $1,801,097 (FY 2019, 2020 and 2021 allocations), notified February 15, 2023. The ConPlan lists $1,361,913 remaining for housing. The 2026 Housing Element estimates $1,455,181 available from award years 2021-2023, earmarked for housing construction and rehabilitation.
record.affordability_requirement: The plan funds affordable rental development or rehabilitation (generally at or below 60% to 80% AMI under HCD PLHA guidelines) and homeless services. The City has not published its own income targets.
record.next_deadline: unknown, verify with agency. No open City solicitation found as of 2026-11-08. The 2019-2023 plan period has ended, so check whether a new five-year plan has been adopted for later allocations.
record.layering_notes: The largest uncommitted local pool identified for the City of Madera (about $1.36M to $1.46M). Pair it with City HOME (separate record) to form one local gap layer. Madera County has its own PLHA allocation (county record), so a project in the city could in principle seek both. State-source funds generally count as public funds under Labor Code 1720. The City web page describes only the 2022 application and award; no commitment to a specific project was found this pass.
record.cycle_notes: no City NOFA found; Council approves commitments
record.prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific rule found. HCD PLHA Final Guidelines (2019) and 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines contain no prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon or Labor Code 1720 provisions, and the City PLHA page does not mention labor standards. Coverage would rest only on the general Labor Code 1720(b) public-funds definition, with the outcome depending on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.
record.audit_note: Tier 3: left unclear. PLHA guidelines (2019 and 2024-2028) searched for prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon, Labor Code and 1720 with no hits; only basis would be Labor Code 1720(b) generally, which depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.
